original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md:33-39: forge test output for four tests, each failing on the commit before E16 and passing after. The S4 test (lines 38-39): in a two-asset channel with one asset's token made to revert on transfer, transfer(assetIndex) still pays the other asset, and transferAllAssets reverts as a whole.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. On integrated d51ae19, forge test runs 38 tests in 8 suites. git grep over test/*.t.sol finds no reference to RevertingTransferToken or ToggleableERC20. The .t.sol calls of transferAllAssets (test/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.t.sol:168, 198, 227; test/ReentryGuard.t.sol:163) use no such token. test/helpers/RevertingTransferToken.sol exists, and script/CheckSettlePerAssetSetup.s.sol is its only user.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. 1. In armada-nitro at d51ae19 run git grep -lE 'RevertingTransferToken|ToggleableERC20' -- 'test/*.t.sol': no output. 2. Run git grep -n transferAllAssets -- 'test/*.t.sol' and read each call's token setup. 3. Run forge test and list the suites.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) armada-nitro forge suite (test/)
restatement: The armada-nitro forge test suite must gain a test that proves the S4 per-asset-exit invariant named in docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md:38-39 (invariant I5): in a two-asset channel where one asset's token is made to revert on transfer, calling transfer(assetIndex) still pays out the other (non-reverting) asset, and calling transferAllAssets reverts as a whole instead of partially succeeding. This proof does not exist today: on commit d51ae19, forge test runs 38 tests across 8 suites, a grep of test/*.t.sol for RevertingTransferToken or ToggleableERC20 finds no match, and the existing transferAllAssets call sites (test/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.t.sol:168,198,227; test/ReentryGuard.t.sol:163) set up tokens that never revert on transfer. The helper contract test/helpers/RevertingTransferToken.sol already exists but is used only by script/CheckSettlePerAssetSetup.s.sol, never by a .t.sol test. The doc states no contract change is expected for S4 (the behavior already exists); the gap is purely missing test coverage.

restatement_clauses.text: In a two-asset channel with one asset's token made to revert on transfer, transfer(assetIndex) still pays the other asset.
In that same two-asset channel scenario, transferAllAssets reverts as a whole.

goal: Add forge test coverage proving that, in a two-asset channel with one asset's token forced to revert on transfer, transfer(assetIndex) still pays the other asset and transferAllAssets reverts as a whole.
acceptance_criteria: Set up a channel holding two different assets, force the token for one of them to revert on every transfer, then exit only the other asset through the single-asset exit path. Check that the other asset is still paid out correctly.

Using the same two-asset channel, with one asset's token forced to revert on every transfer, call the all-assets exit for the whole channel. Check that the call reverts as a whole, with no partial payout.
